07_marg770: These are the words which Moses spoke, etc. The beginning of Deuteronomy seems to be the title of the whole work, because it indicates the person of the author, and what he did, and the place and the time. The name of the book too shows the grace of the New Testament. For Deuteronomy is interpreted "second law", and signifies the Gospel, which explains spiritually the sacraments of the Old Testament; as the book of Deuteronomy is a repetition of the four books of the law. For those contain their own matters in themselves; this one goes over them all again. It has its own sacraments too.
07_marg771: These are the words which Moses spoke, etc. He says this of himself as of another, after the manner of Holy Scripture; as there too: "Moses was the meekest of all men that dwelt upon earth." For so he avoids arrogance and shows that it is to be avoided. Likewise Job too says of himself: "There was a man in the land of Hus, whose name was Job" etc. And John: "This is that disciple who giveth testimony of these things" etc.
07_marg772: He speaks of himself as of another, as John says of himself: "The disciple whom Jesus loved." Or the Holy Ghost bears witness to him, that no one might be able to doubt that Moses wrote these things.
07_marg773: It is asked why he said "these are the words which Moses spoke" and did not say "which God spoke"? And why he commands this book to be put in the ark and not the other books, in which are the words of the Lord? Again, how could he speak those words to all Israel, when so great a multitude was there to be cared for? Answer: he said this to show that he spoke to the people the same words which the Lord spoke to Moses. To the second it must be said that the books, in so far as they are the words of the Lord, need no commendation; but the book of Moses needed letters of commendation. For the Lord wishes the sayings of his own to be held in veneration, and not only his. And because this book is more expressive of the Gospel, therefore it is commanded to be put in the ark and held in greater reverence. To the third question: that Moses spoke to some and commanded them to speak to others; as it is said in Mark 9: "what I say to one, I say to all."

07_marg778: Pharan: increased; Thophel: insipidity; Laban: whitening; Haseroth: courts. For the people was increased in the number of men by the doctrine of the law and the prophets; but it was insipid, because it did not have the salt of wisdom; and whitened by the ceremonies of the law and various cleannesses, which it believed it had from the letter of the law. Which is well signified by the courts, as prepared by the divine scriptures for the entrance of faith. Whence many at the coming of Christ more easily received him whom they recognized as foretold before. Whence Philip: "We have found him of whom Moses in the law and the prophets did write, Jesus the son of Joseph of Nazareth."
07_marg779: The law explained by Moses in eleven days signifies the transgression of the Jewish people in the commandments of the Decalogue. The eleven days are the eleven apostles, through whom, Judas having been rejected, the Gospel of Christ was preached in the world.

07_marg780: Who too, beginning from Horeb, passing through Seir, that is, "hairy" and "filthy", the people [being filthy] with vices, came to Cadesbarne, which is interpreted "changed" or "chosen" or "noble"; signifying the literal sense of the law changed into the spiritual through the Gospel. "For all these things happened to them in figure, and they are written for our correction, upon whom the ends of the world are come." For the law is not dissolved but fulfilled; nor "shall one jot or one tittle pass, till all be fulfilled."
07_marg781: IN THE FORTIETH YEAR, etc. ISIDORE. Allegorically, the forty years, which having been laboriously passed through, the children of Israel crossed over to the promised land, signify the whole time of this world, in which the Church, under labours and perilous temptations, by hoping waits with patience for what it does not see, until it comes to the promised fatherland. Therefore the Lord fasted forty days and was tempted forty nights in the wilderness. For the body of Christ, which is the Church, passes through temptations and labours until it comes to consolation. And that the clothing of the Israelites was corrupted by no age through so many years, and the skins of their shoes lasted without flaw, signifies the incorruptibility of bodies, when the things now corruptible shall remain without corruption.
07_marg782: The number forty is signified, or consists, of ten and four, and signifies the fulfilment of both the law and the Gospel; for ten pertains to the law, but four to the Gospel.
07_marg783: IN THE ELEVENTH, etc. As in the eleventh the transgression of the law is expressed, so in the first day the watchful intent of the lawgiver to teach; who, from the time that the disobedient people did not fear to transgress the law, at once studied to make known the will of the Lord by preaching and correcting, and did not cease to draw or provoke them to better things by words and examples.

07_marg784: AFTER THAT HE HAD SLAIN SEHON KING OF THE AMORRHITES, etc. It is to be noted that, the two kings of the Amorrhites having been slain, the law is recapitulated and the people instructed; because, stumblingblocks having been removed and the troops of vices overcome, one is fittingly trained in doctrine, and the light of faith is opened to those who worthily desire it.
07_marg785: We ought first to slay the vices in ourselves, and so hand on the divine commandments to the peoples.
07_marg786: ISIDORE. Allegorically: in these kings, although the deed done is known, yet through the interpretations of the names a spiritual signification is intimated. For Sehon is interpreted "useless sprout" or "temptation of the eyes", by whom the devil is figured, who transforms himself into an angel of light, that by schisms or heresy he may deceive the unwary. Him the Amorrhites, that is, the embittering, have as king. For unless some pretence goes before, there will be neither heresies of the embittering nor schisms of the provoking. He is slain in each one when pretence is condemned and truth is loved. But Og is interpreted "shutting in", Basan "confusion". For the devil does this, that he may shut off the way to God, setting idolatry in the way, lest anyone believe in Christ. For shutting in goes before as king, confusion follows as people. For those whom he shuts out from the faith of Christ will be confounded when Christ appears. And Sehon dwelt in Hesebon, because the devil, the king of vices, mingles himself with human thoughts and girds the mind with superfluous cares, lest it utter words of truth or exercise works of godliness. For Hesebon is interpreted "thought" or "girdle of grief". Og too, king of Basan, dwelt in Astaroth and Edrai. For Astaroth [means] courts; Edrai, flood of evils; they sound unbelief, namely with wicked works. For the devil strives for this: that those whom he rules may never enter the door of faith, but, remaining outside, may always be busy with wicked works.

07_marg788: THE LORD OUR GOD, etc. In the book of Numbers the departure of the children of Israel from the desert of Sinai is related, but the Lord's command to Moses about the same passage is not told, but only of the cloud which covered the tabernacle, and, when they were to set out, withdrew and went before to the place of pitching the camp. For so it is written: "In the second year, in the second month, the twentieth day of the month, the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle of the covenant, and rested in the wilderness of Pharan." But it is manifest that that passage was ordered by God's command, though it is not mentioned there. Whence elsewhere in the book of Numbers: at the command of the Lord they pitched their tents, and at his command they took them down.
07_marg789: YOU HAVE STAYED LONG ENOUGH, etc. Moses is commanded to withdraw from the mountain on which he had received the law; because the teacher ought not always to be intent on contemplation, but should sometimes come down to take care of himself and his neighbours. Whence: "For whether we be transported in mind, it is to God; or whether we be sober, it is for you."
07_marg790: Not all the things that are in a harp sound, but all help. So not the whole history sounds a spiritual understanding, but the whole helps. For unless the other things stood around, the things that sound spiritually would not stand out.
07_marg791: AND I SAID TO YOU AT THAT TIME, etc. Of this division of powers it is written in Exodus, before they came to mount Sinai, that "Jethro the priest of Madian, the kinsman of Moses", suggested it to him. Whence it is rightly asked how these things agree with each other in manner and time. But what is said here, that Moses said at that time: I alone am not able to bear you, etc., does not signify the time at which they set out from Horeb, but the whole time in which, having set out from Egypt, they tarried in the wilderness. And Moses persuaded his people of these things not by his own counsel but by his kinsman's.
07_marg792: The saints do all things "in due time"; God too, namely: "When the fulness of the time was come, he sent his Son."

It seems to be signified that a mind too intent on human actions is in some way emptied of God, by whom it is made the fuller the more freely it stretches out to things above and eternal.

07_marg806: AND WHEN WE WERE COME INTO CADESBARNE, etc. That in the second year of its going out the people came into the desert of Pharan, which is Cades, where, the spies having returned with the fruits of the land and announcing what they had seen, they murmured against Moses and Aaron, and therefore, afflicted with the weariness of a long journey and with mortality, they perished: this place will give manifest judgment. Where it is to be noted that the forty-two mansions which they had from Egypt as far as the Jordan seem to fit only three courses of years, namely the first, the second, and the fortieth of the going out of Egypt. The first, by a certain distinction, contains twelve: the first, Ramesses, entered on the fifteenth day of the first month; the last, the wilderness of Sinai, reached on the first day of the third month, and not left for eleven continuous months for the sake of building the tabernacle and teaching the law. Of which twelve mansions only nine are expressed by name in Exodus; three are signified without distinction under the name of the desert of Sin (which is said to be between Elim and Sinai). The second year comprises twenty-one mansions; of which, all being comprehended without distinction in the order of the history under the name of the wilderness of Pharan, only the first and second and last, that is, the graves of lust, Haseroth, and Cades, are distinguished by name. But in the catalogue of mansions all alike are shown, how many they are in number, or by what name they are called. The first mansion, that is, the graves of lust, was entered in the second month of the same second year, on the twenty-second day of the month. For in the second year (as the scripture says), in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, they moved the camp from the desert of Sinai, and the cloud rested in the wilderness of Pharan. They set out from the mountain of the Lord a journey of three days, until they came to the place of the mansion which, by the merit of the people lusting for flesh, received the name of the graves of lust. On what day or month of the same year the last of these, that is, Cades, was entered is not said; yet that it lies in the wilderness of Pharan, because it was reached in the same year, is not passed over in silence. For it is written: The people did not move from that place until Mary was called back. And setting out from Haseroth, having pitched their tents in the desert of Pharan, where the Lord spoke to Moses, saying: Send men to view the land of Chanaan. Which, lest it be thought commanded and done at the very next mansion after Haseroth, [it is shown] fulfilled in the last of those which are contained under the name of Pharan. Below it is written: "And the spies of the land, returning after forty days, having gone round the whole country", came to Moses in Pharan, which is Cades. In Deuteronomy too Moses says to the people: When you were come into Cadesbarne I said to you: You are come to the mountain of the Amorrhite, etc. And you said: "Let us send men who may view the land" etc. And that they reached the same mansion in the second year of their going out, from which yet, by the sin of murmuring, they deserved to turn back and wander long through the desert and fall here and there, Moses bears witness in what follows, saying: You abode in Cadesbarne a long time; and setting out thence we came into the wilderness that leadeth to the Red Sea, as the Lord had said to me; and we compassed mount Seir a long time. And below: The time that we walked from Cadesbarne to the torrent Zared was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of the men of war was consumed. And Zared is not the name of any mansion of the forty-two, but of a torrent, to which (as is read in the book of Numbers), having passed the thirty-eighth mansion, named Ijeabarim, they came; leaving which, he says, they camped over against the Arnon, which is in the desert and juts out in the borders of the Amorrhite; which it is not hidden was done in the fortieth year. This last [year] contains ten mansions of the very long way through the desert; of which the first, regained with great labour, is the same, namely that Cades of the desert of Sin, which thirty-eight years before, their fault requiring it, they left behind them, turning back; of which it is written: "The children of Israel came into the desert of Sin in the first month, and the people abode in Cades; and Mary died there, and was buried in the same place. And when the people wanted water, they came together against Moses and Aaron" etc., as far as this: "This is the water of contradiction" etc. It is to be noted that the same Cades is set both in the desert of Pharan and in the desert of Sin, as the scripture relates; whence we conjecture that the part of the desert of Pharan where Cades is is specially called Sin. But this Sin is not that which they passed through as soon as they had crossed the Red Sea, between Elim and Sinai, but another altogether, and written among the Hebrews with other letters. The second mansion of the same fortieth year is mount Hor, on which Aaron died on the first day of the fifth month; the last, the plains of Moab upon the Jordan over against Jericho, where they abode meditating Deuteronomy until, Moses being dead, under Josue as leader they crossed the Jordan on the first day of the tenth month. The mansions of the first year, then, are twelve, of the second twenty-one; of the last ten, that twenty-first, which is Cades, being itself one, and nine others; together, in all, forty-two.
07_marg807: AND YOU CAME TO ME, etc. In the book of Numbers it is written that the Lord said to Moses that he should send men to view the land. But here the people is read to have said: Let us send men to view the land. But the people suggested this first to Moses; Moses referred the counsel to the Lord, according to whose command he afterwards sent the spies.
07_marg808: I SENT OF YOU TWELVE MEN, etc. ISIDORE. The twelve spies sent to spy out the fertile land, who terrified the people, bear the figure of the scribes and Pharisees. For as those were sent by Moses to view carefully the fertile land, so these by the law and the prophets, that through the searching of scripture they might watch for the coming of Christ, in whom was the land, that is, the holy flesh, in which they might obtain the kingdom of God and the fertility of spiritual fruits, and life eternal. But as those terrified the people with despair, lest they trust in God's promise, so the scribes and Pharisees persuaded the people not to believe in Christ, returning to the Egypt of this world, rejecting the manna of faith, seeking the black pots of sins and the rotten onions of blasphemers and the melons withering with the corruption of vices and lusts. And the cluster which two carried is Christ hanging on the wood of the cross, promised to the Gentiles, brought from the land of promise, from the womb of the virgin. The two bearers who go under the burden of the cluster are the two peoples. The former, the Jewish, blind and turned away, ignorant of the grace of him who hangs, and pressed by the burden of the one suspended, is put under it as he judges, according to that: "Let their eyes be darkened that they see not, and bow down their back always." But the latter, the Gentile, believing in Christ, having him always before his eyes, and following as a servant his Lord and a disciple his master, and hearing that saying of the Gospel: "If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me." This is the cluster which poured out the wine of its blood for our salvation in the crushing of the cross, and gave the Church to drink the pressed cup of its passion. This is the cluster which the pomegranates, that is, mother Church, followed; having a number of grains, that is, a multitude of peoples, and the redness of the blood of Christ glittering with its seal; it has also distinct grains, namely divers charisms. Judging themselves unworthy of all these, the unbelievers would not receive the land of the flesh of Christ flowing with milk and honey; which his servants, that is, the Christians, have obtained, of whose doctrine the Church sings: "How sweet are thy words to my palate! more than honey to my mouth." And the fig signifies the law, as the cluster bears the figure of the Saviour; because neither is Christ without the law, nor the law without Christ.

07_marg815: NEITHER IS IT TO BE WONDERED AT, etc. Here Moses says that the Lord, angry with him because of the people, said that he should not enter the land of promise; whereas in the book of Numbers it is read: "The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Because you have not believed me, to sanctify me before the children of Israel, you shall not bring these people into the land which I will give them." But the following sentence seems to solve the question: "This, he says, is the water of contradiction, where the children of Israel strove with words against the Lord" etc. For the strife and rebellion of the people was the cause of the wrath and vengeance both against the people and against Moses and Aaron.

07_marg816: ISIDORE. In Mary prophecy seems to have died; in Moses and Aaron, the law and priesthood of the Jews, who could not go up to the land of promise nor lead the believing people out of the wilderness of this world; but only Jesus, that is, the Saviour, the true Son of God. In the thirty-third mansion Moses offended the Lord. For, troubled by the murmuring of the people, doubting, he struck the rock, as though God could not give water from the rock, because he had not done so before. Moses in this place bears the figure of the people set under the law. For so the people fastened Christ to the wood of the cross, not believing him to be the power of God; as Moses, when he struck the rock, doubted of the power of God. But from the rock struck water flowed, and the wound of Christ was given back as life to believers. For the rock was Christ. This carnal despair about the divinity of Christ the Lord commands to die in the height of Christ himself, when he commands Moses to die on the mountain. For Christ is the rock, Christ the mountain: the rock, lowly strength; the mountain, towering greatness. Of this mountain it is said: A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid, etc. The prudence of the flesh lives when the humility of Christ on the cross is despised as a rock struck. The prudence of the flesh dies when Christ is acknowledged as exalted, as the eminence of a mountain.

07_marg817: AND WHEN READY ARMED, etc. This sentence strikes at human pride, which presumes on its own strength and does not trust in the power of God. For the Amorrhites, that is, the embittering, are the spiritual enemies who dwell on the mountains of pride and kill the presumptuous from Seir to Horma, that is, from the filth of vices to the damnation of punishments. For Seir is "hairy"; Horma is interpreted "anathema". For whoever does not fear to be polluted with the filth of vices must, according to his merits, be handed over to the fires of Gehenna. For the demons wish to entangle us in earthly desires; and if we persevere in sins and do not cease to go up the mountain of pride, they cut us down with fiery darts and lead us to perpetual anathema. Therefore let us not, after the manner of the Pelagians, presume on our own power, but, considering our infirmity, let us obey the Lord in all things, that, the enemies having been overcome, we may obtain the promised joys of the heavenly fatherland.
07_marg818: We must beware lest, murmuring against the Lord, we go up the mountain of pride, thinking that we can be saved by our own strength; lest we be at once handed over to the Amorrhites, that is, to the demons.

07_marg819: AND DEPARTING, etc. GILBERT. We pass quickly over things expounded in other books, that we may tarry on those that are to be expounded.
07_marg820: Seir is a mountain in the land of Edom, on which Esau dwelt, in the region of Gebalene, where the Horrhite dwelt before, whom Chodorlahomor slew; which received from Esau, hairy and shaggy, the name Seir, that is, "of the hairy one". The Horrhites, like the other nations which those overcame who descended from the seed of the patriarchs, express the wicked spirits or vices, which those can overcome who press on in the footsteps and teachings of the holy fathers and carry on spiritual warfare under Christ the king; of which it is said: "Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers" etc.
07_interl801: it is interpreted "he raised up"; which is now the metropolis
07_marg821: TO THE CHILDREN OF LOT I HAVE GIVEN AR IN POSSESSION, etc. Ar is the metropolis of the Moabites, upon the bank of the torrent Arnon, once possessed by a most ancient nation, the Emims; afterwards held by the children of Lot, that is, the Moabites, the inhabitants having been overthrown. It is shown today on the top of a mountain; but the torrent, coming down through steep places, flows into the Dead Sea. Allegorically. Ar is interpreted "he raised up"; Emims, that is, "the terrible". These are the demons, who raise up strifes and contentions and prepare the darts of wickedness against the faithful. The Enacims too, begotten of the stock of Enac and equalled to the giants in tallness, according to their name signify the demons. For [Enac] is interpreted "necklace on a lofty neck". For, lifted up with the haughtiness of pride, they ascribe all the equipment of their warfare to their own strength. Therefore they easily yield to those who trust in the strength of God and say with the Psalmist: "The Lord is my strength and my praise" etc.
07_interl806: horrible in the hugeness of their bodies
07_marg822: FROM CADESBARNE, etc. JEROME. Cadesbarne is a place in the desert which is joined to the city of Petra in Arabia, where Mary died, and Moses, the rock having been struck, gave water to the thirsting people. The tomb of Mary is shown there even today; and the princes of Amalec too were slain there by Chodorlahomor.
07_marg823: SO I SENT MESSENGERS, etc. Allegorically. Sehon signifies the devil, for [the name] is "useless sprout" or "unfruitful tree" or "lifted up". Israel [signifies] the Christian people, which desires to pass through the way of this world and come to the heavenly kingdoms. This people sends to Sehon, promising with peaceable words that it will not dwell in his land, but only pass through and go by the king's way. This each one promised when he first came to the water of baptism and received the first seals of the faith. For he renounced the devil and his pomps and works and all his service and pleasures. This is what is said: "that Israel will not turn aside into his field or into his vineyard, and will not drink water from his cistern"; that is, will no longer take up the discipline either of astrology or of magic or of any doctrine that is against godliness. But he will drink from the fountains of the Saviour; he will not forsake the fountain of living water to drink from the fountain of Sehon; but he will go by the king's way, which is Christ, who says: "I am the way, the truth and the life", and the King, according to that: "Give to the king thy judgment, O God." He will not turn aside into his field or into his vineyard; to his works, namely, or to his wicked senses. The Amorrhites are interpreted "speaking" or "embittering", because they provoke God to bitterness and trust only in words, like the poets, astrologers, philosophers, who speak empty things. But the kingdom of God is not in speech, but in power. The faithful wish to pass through in peace, and to be peaceable even with the enemies of peace; although they offend the prince of the world the more, the more they say they do not wish to tarry with him nor touch anything of his. Thence, exasperated, he persecutes the more, stirs up dangers, threatens tortures, gathers his people, demands to fight against Israel. His people are the princes and judges of the world and all the ministers of wickedness, who persecute the people of God. But he too comes into Jasa, which is interpreted "fulfilment of the commandment". For he who has come to the fulfilment of God's commandments will not fear Sehon or his raging army. For to fulfil the commandments of God is to overcome the devil and his army. For so God crushes Satan under our feet and gives us power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy.

07_marg824: By long patience, not correcting. Whence in Exodus: "I have hardened the heart of Pharao"; and in the Psalm: "He turned their heart to hate his people." And the cause of the hardening is added: that he might be delivered into thy hands, that is, that he might be crushed by thee; which would not happen unless he resisted, nor would he resist unless he were hardened. If we seek the justice of this thing, his judgments are unsearchable; but there is no iniquity with God.

07_marg825: AND WE SLEW HIM WITH HIS SONS, etc. These are the true Israelites, not in the flesh but in the spirit. They dwell in all the cities of the Amorrhites, since the churches of Christ are spread through the whole world; and each of us was a city of king Sehon, because folly, pride, impiety and all that the devil suggests reigned in us. But when the strong one was conquered and his vessels plundered, we were made cities of Israel, the inheritance of the saints; the unfruitful tree having first been cut down and the lifted-up king cast down, and the meek one reigning in us, who says: "Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart" etc. The names of the places too agree. For Aroer is interpreted "lifting up", Arnon "heap of testimony". From Aroer, then, which is upon the bank of the torrent Arnon, etc.: because every person of whatever dignity, trusting in the state of pride or in worldly pomp, with the persecutors who straiten Christians with various tribulations, as far as the conventicles of heretics, who fight against the Church with depraved testimonies of the scriptures, but cannot prevail to resist, are delivered conquered into the hands of the saints, with their dwellings.
